thread:
Oncall Bot: PAGERS — KV cache pressure spike in us-west-2 / rope service. Sudden increase in prefix cache evictions and continuous batch latency. Error rate up 6x.
Maria Chen: seeing the same in dashboards, rope nodes showing sustained >95% mem and kernel OOMs on some gpus. Possibly related to the new YaRN sliding-window prefetch rollout we did at 03:10 UTC.
Aj Patel: can we toggle the prefetch flag off? which job flipped it?
Samir Reddy: rollout id yarn-prefetch-v2 -> started 03:08; target 20% of nodes. Metrics show control -> 0.7r/s, experiment -> 12r/s on longctx requests.
Tess Nguyen: that's the perf cliff we've been worried about. Prefetch is pulling large KV prefixes into memory per-request, causing continuous batching to expand KV cardinality and thrash.
Maria Chen: immediate mitigation: set feature flag yarn_sliding_prefetch = false for the cluster and reduce continuous_batch_max_tokens to 512. I'm going to push now.
Maria Chen: /deploybot run flag-update --cluster us-west-2 --flag yarn_sliding_prefetch=false
Deploy Bot: Command received: flag-update yarn_sliding_prefetch=false on us-west-2. Patch applied to control plane.
Deploy Bot: Flag update completed in 18s, config pushed to 100% of control plane proxies.
Aj Patel: reducing batch config: updating serving config -> continuous_batch_max_tokens: 4096 -> 512, continuous_batch_max_items: 64 -> 16
Samir Reddy: pushed batch config via configroll 2026-03-15T03:24Z
Samir Reddy: dropping prefetch reduced immediate memory pressure, but we still have elevated KV cardinality from already-prefetched keys. Need eviction hard-limit and graceful KV GC.
Maria Chen: running eviction: curl -X POST 'https://ops-api/redwood/kv/evict' -d '{"cluster":"us-west-2","policy":"aggressive","percent":30}'
Maria Chen: evict call returned 202, jobs scheduled across nodes.
Tess Nguyen: patch in runtime to bail prefetch early for >NTK=131k and longctx>8k to stop large prefixes being pulled. Will push hotfix to canary.
Deploy Bot: Canary deployment of runtime-hotfix-prefetch-bailout -> 3 nodes.
Samir Reddy: canary shows 70% reduction in avg kv-set per request and memory trending down. Latency 95p back to normal for canary.
Luis (CSE): FYI, two customers (enterprise-omega, fintech-sparrow) reported latency spikes on multi-turn chat. CS team notified and doing callbacks.
Priya R.: I'm taking handoff at 04:00 UTC. Summary for next oncall: yarn sliding prefetch caused a prefetch storm on long-context routes; we disabled flag, reduced batch sizes, evicted 30% cached prefixes, canary runtime fix looks good. Continuing: verify full rollout of runtime fix, monitor evictions and tail latency, open postmortem draft.
Maria Chen: agree. I'll create incident-ticket and add dashboards + heap dump links. Also capture sample request ID list for regression tests.
Aj Patel: action items: 1) finish runtime rollout (Samir), 2) expand eviction if mem doesn't continue trending down (Maria), 3) run offline eval to reproduce prefetched prefix size distribution (Tess), 4) CS comms update (Luis).
Oncall Bot: Handoff scheduled: Priya R. assigned. Pager cleared for first responder. If regressions reappear, escalate to infra-eng.
Priya R.: got it. I'll post a short writeup and start a postmortem template. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
